newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end mixed, platinum higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end mixed, platinum higher.

text.p: Tokyo gold futures ended mixed on Thursday, as the weaker yen offset continued declines in gold bullion prices, traders said, while platinum ended higher.
TOCOM yen-based gold futures ranged from one yen lower to five yen higher at the close, with the benchmark December contract steady at 1,326 yen per gram.
Local investors liquidated long gold futures positions, traders said, while trade houses bought futures and sold bullion in arbitrage trade.
Spot gold was quoted at $349.30/80 per ounce at Tokyo's Thursday close, against $350.50/00 in New York on Wednesday.
Local investors, who use shares as collateral for their TOCOM positions, were liquidating longs after the recent slump in the Japanese stock market, traders said.
They added that local investors were discouraged by the slide in bullion, which sank overnight to new three-year lows, and they may become active sellers if the yen turns firmer.
Yen-based platinum futures were higher in all months, up two to eight yen, with the benchmark December contract five yen firmer at 1,346 yen per gram.
Palladium futures were mixed, with most-active December down one yen at 457 yen per gram.

Local traders are carefully watching to see if Russia approves its 1997 budget on Friday, thus eliminating a key obstacle standing in the way of talks with Japan over this year's palladium supply contracts.

Japan-Russia talks on one-year supply contracts for palladium and other platinum group metals, usually held in mid-December, were postponed indefinitely last month due in part to a delay in the Russian budget.
Silver futures were higher, with benchmark December up 1.0 yen at 180.2 yen per 10 grams.
